What it means: Applicants, applied quantity, and final tranches describe demand and supply.
Possible research use: Calculate macro allocation rates. Link exact tier rules to application returns. Test the allocation-return relation.

What it means: Public holding includes eligible holdings. Unrestricted holding measures available supply under the stored definition.
Possible research use: Study liquidity and price pressure. Keep the denominator and locked holdings explicit.

What it means: HSI returns, HIBOR, bank balances, and recent IPO counts describe conditions before the offer.
Possible research use: Control for market returns, funding conditions, and offer waves. Use only information known at the test date.

What it means: Mechanism and regime fields classify the offer and settlement setting.
Possible research use: Compare mechanisms when they differ. A constant regime flag cannot identify an effect within 2026.

What it means: Opening and closing prices, volume, and turnover describe listing-day trading.
Possible research use: Study price discovery and trading intensity. The flipping ratio is a volume proxy, not investor-level selling.

What it means: Later prices and index benchmarks separate the IPO jump from later trading returns.
Known N: One month: 102. Three months: 82. Six months: 37.
Possible research use: Calculate later returns from the first-day close. Use mature horizons and matched benchmark coverage.

What it means: Purchases, option exercise, and end dates describe price support after listing.
Possible research use: Study support and prices after support ends. These are later outcomes, not ex-ante pricing controls.

What it means: Contract dates and event returns describe changes around investor unlock dates.
Possible research use: Run an event study of price and volume changes. Require contract evidence and complete event windows.
